title: Foundations of Verifiable Rewards
summary: Work through Foundations of Verifiable Rewards.

blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **Foundations of Verifiable Rewards**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

blocks.source: Vol III, Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards, § Foundations of Verifiable Rewards
blocks.md: Starting from `trained_policy_v1` (a later section), the repair agent can already propose tool calls and edits when dispatched on a version-conflict bug for which no curated recovery exists. Whereas behavioral cloning (supervised imitation of recorded actions) stalls the moment a trajectory leaves the demonstrated corpus, reinforcement learning executes candidate rollouts in the live container environment and scores the resulting trajectories against programmatic checks. The supervised checkpoint serves only to bootstrap sampling; once exploration begins, optimization depends entirely on the agent's ability to act, observe, and receive an evaluative score.

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Reward as measurement matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: The false-accept share of rewarded rollouts moves with the policy's current pass rate rather than being a fixed verifier property, so reward shaping must preserve the priority of correct outcomes.

questions.q: The section **Foundations of Verifiable Rewards** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Ratios and gradients are valid only on per-invocation records of the delivered prefix token IDs, sampled token IDs, and behavior log probabilities under the actual sampling transforms.

GRPO replaces the learned critic with G rollouts per task and broadcasts one standardized coefficient to every sampled token of a rollout, and its clipping and KL estimator choices change how that signal is weighted.
A terminal reward gives every turn the same reward-to-go, so separating a useful step from a faulty one is bought with a critic, more samples, or step-level signals, each at its own cost.
The false-accept share of rewarded rollouts moves with the policy's current pass rate rather than being a fixed verifier property, so reward shaping must preserve the priority of correct outcomes.
questions.hint: Re-read the excerpt and the section map: which idea is this section building toward?
questions.explanation: This section develops **Reward as measurement**: The false-accept share of rewarded rollouts moves with the policy's current pass rate rather than being a fixed verifier property, so reward shaping must preserve the priority of correct outcomes.

questions.q: True or false: in the book's concept map, *Reward as measurement* must align reward with *Task acceptance contract*.

questions.explanation: True. Reward as measurement must align reward with Task acceptance contract.
